title: Sixteen Missing Bars  (缺失的十六小节)

segments.t: 当星期天的夕阳将院子里的灯笼染成金色时，伊芙琳小姐坐在走廊的桌旁，面前放着五线谱纸和一支软铅笔，而卡莱布则为她和汉娜端来热薄荷茶。让我们先来听听整个场景。
Tessa sent hot mint tea and warm almond biscuits for our composer!
Thank you both. Listen while I tap two rhythms on the table.
Does the ending go fast and bright, or gentle and slow?
Arthur's aunt wrote a light dancing beginning, like morning footsteps.
Then in the middle, the melody climbs up like afternoon conversation!
Exactly! So at six in the evening, how should a Friday waltz end?
Warm and unhurried, like friends lingering over their last cup of tea.
Yes! Repeat the opening four notes softly, one octave higher, and come home.
Just hearing you hum it in this glass room sounds wonderful, Evelyn!
Wait, right in bar twenty-eight, the melody lands squarely on middle D!
The exact silent key Graham is repairing tomorrow morning!
No pressure for poor Graham. The whole song rests on his tweezers!
现在让我们慢慢重温每一句。
Tessa sent hot mint tea and warm almond biscuits for our composer!
“泰莎为我们的作曲家送来了热薄荷茶和温热的杏仁饼干！”注意配料是如何放在菜肴或饮料前面的，
warm almond biscuits
就像在 hot mint tea 中一样。
Thank you both. Listen while I tap two rhythms on the table.
“谢谢你们俩。听着，我在桌上用手指敲出两个节奏。”用手指在木头上轻轻而有节奏地敲击，用动词 tap 来表示：
tap two rhythms
而 Thank you both 则是同时感谢两个人。
Does the ending go fast and bright, or gentle and slow?
“结尾是快而明快，还是轻柔而缓慢？”要询问一段音乐是如何推进或发展的，用动词 go 加上形容词非常合适：
go fast and bright,
用来描述结尾的特点。
Arthur's aunt wrote a light dancing beginning, like morning footsteps.
“阿瑟的姑姑写了一个轻盈跳跃的开头，就像早晨的脚步声。”人走路时脚步的声音用复合词来表示：
morning footsteps.
将 foot（脚）和 step（步）结合起来。
Then in the middle, the melody climbs up like afternoon conversation!
“然后在中间部分，旋律像午后的交谈一样上升！”当音符向更高的音调攀升时，... 的视觉意象：
climbs up
让人感受到音乐是如何增强的。
Exactly! So at six in the evening, how should a Friday waltz end?
“没错！那么在下午六点，星期五的圆舞曲应该如何结尾呢？”要询问关于最和谐或最合适的建议，可以使用情态动词 should：
how should a Friday waltz end?
邀请人们想象茶室的氛围。
Warm and unhurried, like friends lingering over their last cup of tea.
“温暖而从容，就像朋友们在最后一杯茶前流连忘返。”纯粹出于喜欢而多留一会儿不想离开，集中体现在动词 linger 上：
lingering over
伴随着优美的形容词 unhurried，不慌不忙的。
Yes! Repeat the opening four notes softly, one octave higher, and come home.
“对！轻轻地重复开头的四个音符，高一个八度，然后回家。”在音乐中，通过回到静止的主音来解决旋律，这种充满诗意的表达方式是：
one octave higher, and come home.
为圆舞曲画上圆满的句号。
Just hearing you hum it in this glass room sounds wonderful, Evelyn!
“伊芙琳，光是在这个玻璃房间里听你哼唱就觉得太棒了！”前面带有 just 的动名词在句子中作整个句子的主语：
Just hearing you hum it
在 hearing 后面，hum 保持原形。
Wait, right in bar twenty-eight, the melody lands squarely on middle D!
“等等，就在第二十八小节，旋律不偏不倚地落在中央 D 上！”要说明一个音符或节拍准确无误地落在中心，land 会与副词 squarely 结合使用：
lands squarely on middle D!
由 square 派生而来。
The exact silent key Graham is repairing tomorrow morning!
“正好就是格雷厄姆明天早上要修的那颗哑键！”放在名词前面，
The exact silent key
强调了与待办任务的巧合。
No pressure for poor Graham. The whole song rests on his tweezers!
“可怜的格雷厄姆没有压力。整首歌都全靠他的镊子了！”当某件事的成功完全取决于一个细节时，动词 rest 与 on 搭配在...中大放异彩：
rests on his tweezers!
以 No pressure（没有压力）的玩笑作为结尾。让我们把整个场景连起来再听一遍。
Tessa sent hot mint tea and warm almond biscuits for our composer!
Thank you both. Listen while I tap two rhythms on the table.
Does the ending go fast and bright, or gentle and slow?
Arthur's aunt wrote a light dancing beginning, like morning footsteps.
Then in the middle, the melody climbs up like afternoon conversation!
Exactly! So at six in the evening, how should a Friday waltz end?
Warm and unhurried, like friends lingering over their last cup of tea.
Yes! Repeat the opening four notes softly, one octave higher, and come home.
Just hearing you hum it in this glass room sounds wonderful, Evelyn!
Wait, right in bar twenty-eight, the melody lands squarely on middle D!
The exact silent key Graham is repairing tomorrow morning!
No pressure for poor Graham. The whole song rests on his tweezers!
伊芙琳小姐用铅笔草拟了一个充满温情的结尾，其中决定性的音符稳稳地落在中央 D 上。现在我们去厨房进行菜单试菜吧。
Have a nice evening!
